name: centrifugal_air_compressor_power
title: Centrifugal air compressor power (example 5.14)
summary: Teaching example of the power of a gas-turbine centrifugal air compressor, from the steady-flow energy balance with outlet kinetic energy. Inlet kinetic energy and potential energy are neglected.

origin.course: ULiège, thermodynamique appliquée, THD10 repetition 2, 2017-2018, example 5.14

verification.summary: Against the stored solution of R2_E6_borguet.EES with compare_solution.py --ees-units: 9 common variables, 2 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 0. h_in and h_out carry the ideal-gas Air reference offset (CoolSolve - EES = 125.868 kJ/kg and 126.047 kJ/kg). Power is 2.81306e6 W versus 2.81036e6 W (rel 9.58e-04).
verification.reference: EES stored solution in R2_E6_borguet.EES (9 variables, EES X8.423), compared with compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: Largest relative difference printed by compare_solution.py --ees-units is 2.95e-01 on h_in (426298 J/kg vs 300430 J/kg); h_out is 2.07e-01. Unrounded values: h_in 0.295258, h_out 0.207031. CoolSolve - EES is +125867.8 J/kg at 26.85 °C and +126047.5 J/kg at 206.85 °C (the documented ideal-gas Air offset is about -126 kJ/kg for EES - CoolSolve). The 179.7 J/kg change of that offset is the cp difference; it raises the power by 2696 W (rel 9.58e-04), inside rtol 0.001. Temperatures, pressures, c_out and q_m match exactly. 0 iterations with .initials and 0 without; every block is explicit. Enthalpy guesses are the EES values in J and are not the CoolSolve enthalpies. The AirH2O hint was not followed. The warning that 206.85 is read as °C is the intended unit (480 K).
